articles.title: Every Nintendo Console: A Full History of Release Dates
articles.summary: Did you know Nintendo has had this many consoles?
articles.body:
Nintendo is the most recognizable name in history when it comes to video games. From the beginning, Nintendo has been at the forefront of creativity and innovation in the home console space. Nintendo is known for its vast library of treasured IPs, with many offering the same charm dozens of years later. Now that the Switch 2 has launched into the world, you may be wanting to take a look back at the gaming giant's history in the console space.

Below, we've rounded up every single console Nintendo has ever released. Journey through the ages and discover how Nintendo has continued to push the gaming medium forward!

Looking to save on a new Nintendo Switch or new titles for your system? Be sure to check out the best Nintendo Switch 2 deals available now.

How Many Nintendo Consoles Have There Been?

In total, 33 Nintendo consoles have been released throughout Nintendo's history with the latest being the Switch 2 that released in June 2025. We've included revision models for both home and handheld consoles in this total, which include brandings like XL and Mini.

Every Nintendo Console in Order of Release

The Color TV-Game line of systems was Nintendo's first foray into gaming hardware and one that you might not necessarily be aware of. These devices were a joint venture by Nintendo and Mitsubishi Electronics, with the latter involved as Nintendo was inexperienced at developing hardware. These systems were a major success at the time and ultimately led Nintendo to divert its focus to developing more gaming hardware. Almost 50 years later, the Color TV-Game's legacy is still felt, with Nintendo invested more than ever in gaming.

Nintendo's first foray into the handheld market was with its Game & Watch devices, each loaded with a different game. While you might not think much of it, the Game & Watch series sold more than 40 million units worldwide. These devices brought many gaming revelations that are still utilized today, such as the D-Pad in the Donkey Kong Game & Watch. These consoles made a comeback somewhat recently when Nintendo released limited edition models in 2020 and 2021 to celebrate the anniversaries of Mario and Zelda.

3. Nintendo Entertainment System - October 18, 1985

The Nintendo Entertainment System ( NES ) is the first Nintendo home console to be released in North America. Known as the Family Computer (Famicom) in Japan, this console implemented cartridges to allow users to purchase and play as many games as they'd like on the system. Almost all of the major Nintendo franchises we know and love got their starts here, with series like Super Mario, The Legend of Zelda, and Metroid. Overall, the NES is one of the most important consoles in video game history, as it established a pipeline for generations to come.

The first true Nintendo handheld video game console is the Game Boy , which released in North America during the Summer of 1989. Game Boy took a major step forward from the Game & Watch, offering cartridges so you could play as many games as you'd like on the system. For many, the Game Boy's most well-known game is Tetris, which was bundled in with the system in every region with the exception of Japan. LEGO also recently announced its own plastic brick version of the iconic console .

5. Super Nintendo Entertainment System - August 23, 1991

The Super Nintendo Entertainment System ( SNES ) brought 16-bit graphics to a Nintendo platform for the first time. This console was when Nintendo began crafting major evolutions for their biggest series, with games like Super Mario World , Donkey Kong Country, and more. Despite launching toward the latter part of this console generation, the SNES still managed to be the best-selling console of this time period with its profound software lineup and generational appeal.

The Virtual Boy is quite possibly Nintendo's weirdest console . This portable device was the first-ever video game console that could properly display 3D visuals. Merely 22 games were ever released for the system, with Mario's Tennis, 3D Tetris, and Virtual Boy Wario Land among the most popular. Virtual Boy only lasted on the market for one year, with just under 800,000 units sold in its lifetime.

Nintedo actually brought back the Virtual Boy for the Switch 2 . Games for the 3D device will be locked behind a Nintendo Switch Online + Expansion Pack subscription.

The Game Boy Pocket is a smaller version of the Game Boy, featuring a definitive black-and-white screen instead of the Game Boy's green-tinted display. One of the biggest improvements of this release was the new hardware inside that improved the response time of the display on screen. However, with the smaller design, the Game Boy Pocket had a shorter battery life than the Game Boy.

Nintendo 64 brought 3D graphics to a Nintendo home console for the very first time. This revolutionary device brought two of the most influential titles ever : Super Mario 64 and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time . The N64 completely refreshed what the NES and SNES offered with a bold new controller that featured an analog stick for the first time. N64 is one of the few consoles where Nintendo sold many iconic special editions, with multiple translucent variants available.

Game Boy Light is a console you might not be too familiar with, and a large part of that is likely due to it being exclusive to Japan. This Game Boy revision was bigger than the Game Boy Pocket, but added a new backlight so players could play in low-light areas. Ultimately, this change allowed for the Game Boy Light to feature longer battery life than the Game Boy Pocket, around 20 hours in total.

Game Boy Color finally brought color to a Nintendo handheld. The device was backwards-compatible with all Game Boy games, so it was an easy upgrade for many. Some Game Boy games had support for color already, so titles like Tetris could be experienced anew with bright and beatuiful colors. With the new hardware inside, hundreds of new games were also released exclusively for the system.

Game Boy Advance (GBA) was the first massive technological leap forward in the Game Boy brand for Nintendo. In a major shakeup to the previous Game Boy models, GBA flipped the device orientation to a horizontal, rectangular shape versus the portrait-designed Game Boy. 16-bit graphics were now available portably — a major upgrade from the Game Boy's 8-bit graphics support. Of course, Game Boy and Game Boy Color games were also supported via backwards compatibility. This opened the number of games available on GBA into the thousands.

Pokémon mini released in 2001 with a major focus on Pokémon games (as the name implies). This device is so incredibly small that you can fit multiple in your pocket. Only 10 games were ever released for Pokémon mini, with just four in North America. Pokémon mini featured a built-in clock function, an infrared port for communication, and built-in rumble.

13. Nintendo GameCube - November 18, 2001

Nintendo GameCube built upon the success of the Nintendo 64 and followed up with sequels to many of the beloved titles found on the system. Super Mario Sunshine, The Legend of Zelda: Wind Waker, and Super Smash Bros. Ultimate are all three titles that shined on the system. GameCube made a major departure from Nintendo's prior home consoles, as it utilized discs instead of cartridges. Additionally, the controller made major improvements from N64, with built-in rumble, analog/digital triggers, and a staggered design for the sticks. The legacy of the GameCube still lives on today, with many of the franchises that debuted on the title more popular than ever. (Looking at you, Animal Crossing.)

Some classic GameCube games have been added to Nintendo Switch Online alongside the launch of the Switch 2 . Nintendo has continued to add new titles to its emulator throughout 2026 so far.

Panasonic Q is a collaborative console between Panasonic and Nintendo. This device combined a traditional GameCube with a DVD player, allowing for users to play GameCube titles, watch DVDs, and listen to CDs. Its design is striking, with a stainless steel exterior and a front LCD panel. Due to the steep price and low sales, the console only lasted two years on the market.

15. Game Boy Advance SP - March 23, 2003

Game Boy Advance SP (GBA SP) was the first revision of the Game Boy Advance. A major change from the previous model was the hinge design, which placed the screen on the top panel and the controls on the bottom panel. Additionally, the GBA SP featured a chargeable battery and a backlit screen (exclusive to later models), which were both major improvements from its predecessor. Nintendo opted to omit a headphone jack on this model but offered an adapter for players to listen to audio through headphones.

Nintendo DS was the first unit in the DS line, which marked the start of Nintendo's best-selling console. The DS featured Wi-Fi support for the first time, with a standout clamshell design that expanded upon the Game Boy SP. With two screens, games on Nintendo DS were quite unique, with many developers creating experiences unlike anything on the market previously. The bottom screen was a touchscreen that players could use with the included stylus pen.

Game Boy Micro was famously revealed by Reggie Fils-Aimé during E3 2005 , with many shocked at the small size of the system. The rectangular design featured a D-pad and two buttons on the front, with Start and Select buttons on the bottom side of the unit. Like previous GBA models, Game Boy Micro was backwards compatible with Game Boy and Game Boy Color games, in addition to playing Game Boy Advance titles. Game Boy Micro featured a backlit screen that allowed for adjustable brightness and even lighting across the screen. The system only sold 2.42 million units across 18 months until its production ended.

Nintendo DS Lite was the first revision of the Nintendo DS. This model released just under a year and a half after the initial launch of the Nintendo DS, and it brought a few changes to the fold. First, the DS Lite is slimmer and lighter than its predecessor. The screens are also both noticeably brighter than the standard DS, which made games easier to see regardless of lighting conditions. Lastly, the battery life was much improved on Nintendo DS Lite to allow for more playtime without the need for a charge.

Nintendo Wii marked a huge resurgence for Nintendo's home console business, with a unique focus on motion controls that sold many on the system. The unique Wii Remote relied heavily on motion to control the system, utilizing both infrared and digital technology to input motion from all directions. Nintendo released all sorts of accessories for the system, from the Nunchuk to the Wii MotionPlus. Wii was backwards compatible with both GameCube titles and controllers, since the Wii utilized optical discs once again. One of the defining software offerings of Wii was Virtual Console, which allowed players to purchase NES, SNES, and N64 titles for digital download.

Nintendo DSi made a few changes to the Nintendo DS, acting as the second major revision of the model. It added two cameras, one on the hinge inside and one on the outside panel, which were utilized in games and in certain software. An SD card slot was also added to provide additional storage for downloaded games. Unfortunately, the Nintendo DSi also removed the Game Boy Advance slot that was present on the Nintendo DS and Nintendo DS Lite.

Nintendo DSi XL was a larger model of the DSi that launched a year after the main model. This device featured larger, wide-view screens that both sat at 4.2 inches. Two speakers were added to the top panel to provide better, clearer sound for players, and a bigger battery for longer playtime. With the larger screens, Nintendo DS games were brighter and easier to experience than ever.

Nintendo 3DS was the successor to the Nintendo DS line, offering a wide variety of new features, games, and hardware capabilities. The key feature of 3DS was the 3D capabilities, which were powered by stereoscopy so no eyewear was required. Interestingly enough, this is the same technology that was used to power the Virtual Boy, which only lasted on the market for one year in 1995. 3DS was a massive upgrade from Nintendo DS, with many impressive titles like The Legend of Zelda: A Link Between Worlds, Fire Emblem: Awakening, and Super Mario 3D Land.

Nintendo 3DS XL (known as Nintendo 3DS LL in Japan) featured a screen that was 90% larger than the original 3DS. This console retained every feature of the Nintendo 3DS and simply offered a larger screen. Many games were much easier to view with this model, especially with the bottom screen.

The Nintendo Wii U was the successor to Nintendo Wii, featuring an all-new GamePad controller. This controller featured a screen and could be used to play titles off of the TV. All previous Nintendo Wii games, accessories, and controllers were compatible with the system. Wii U was Nintendo's first-ever console to support HD, which was a major step up from the 480p capabilities of the Wii. There were some incredible titles released for the system, including Xenoblade Chronicles X, Super Mario 3D World, Splatoon, and Bayonetta 2 to name a few. Ultimately, a combination of poor marketing and confusion led to poor sales of the Wii U, which left Nintendo in a crucial state prior to the launch of Nintendo Switch.

25. Nintendo Wii Mini - December 7, 2012

Wii Mini was a smaller, lighter Wii unit that was released at the very tail end of the Wii's life cycle. Wii Mini featured a top-facing disc drive, which was a huge departure from the standard Wii. Additionally, it removed support for GameCube, Wi-Fi connectivity, 480p resolution, and SD cards. This console launched in Canada during December 2012, with releases in Europe and the United States in 2013.

Nintendo 2DS offered exactly what it sounds like: fun, 2D content. This device removed the 3D capability present on 3DS models and instead flattened out the console to a square-like shape. All 3DS titles are playable on 2DS, with all features minus 3D intact. The console did lose considerable sound quality, as the speaker onboard was swapped for a mono speaker versus a stereo speaker. However, with the extremely low price point, Nintendo had to cut costs somewhere.

New Nintendo 3DS made significant upgrades to the standard 3DS, with new controls, features, and platform support. Nintendo added the C-Stick, ZR and ZL buttons, and NFC support for amiibo with this release. While the New Nintendo 3DS launched across Japan, Australia, and Europe in late 2014 to early 2015, North America did not receive this standard version until September 25, 2015.

28. New Nintendo 3DS XL - February 13, 2015

Released before New Nintendo 3DS in North America, New Nintendo 3DS XL was a larger version of the revised 3DS model. Although the standard model did feature bigger screens than the standard 3DS, the 3DS XL had even bigger displays, which allowed for more immersive games. The New 3DS XL made a major change from the smaller model as it removed the ability to change face plates. Many felt this limited customization, though Nintendo did offer mutliple special editions for players to purchase.

Nintendo Switch fully realized the vision of the Wii U and completely propelled Nintendo to the top of the industry once again. The Switch operates as both a home and portable console, with the ability to play games wherever you go. The same grand experiences you were used to on consoles can now be played in a park, on a plane, or in your bed. With arguably the best first-party library of any Nintendo console, Switch has seen some of the greatest games of all time be released on it. There have also been quite a few special edition Nintendo Switch consoles that have been released throughout the years.

New Nintendo 2DS XL was a major update to the 2DS. Additions for this model included an analog stick, shoulder buttons, amiibo support, and more. 2DS XL also moved back to the signature clamshell-hinge design, which was a departure from the flat panel used for 2DS. This console was also able to play New 3DS titles, which included games like Xenoblade Chronicles 3D and Fire Emblem Warriors.

31. Nintendo Switch Lite - September 20, 2019

Nintendo Switch Lite shrunk down the body of the Nintendo Switch, utilizing a 5.5 inch LCD screen. The major change with this model was the removal of Joy-Cons, as the controllers became built-in on the sides of the console. As a result of these changes, the Nintendo Switch Lite is only playable in handheld mode and cannot be docked to a TV. This allowed Nintendo to cut costs and charge $100 less for the Lite model.

32. Nintendo Switch OLED Model - October 8, 2021

Nintendo Switch OLED debuted alongside Metroid Dread in October 2021. This premium Switch increased the size of the screen to 7 inches while also adding a new premium OLED panel. In addition to these features, the speakers and kickstand were also reworked for this device. The OLED model released alongside a new dock, featuring rounded corners and a built-in LAN port.

The newest Nintendo console has arrived. Nintendo has emphasized that the Switch 2 isn't just an upgraded Switch system but an entire redesign, featuring magnetic Joy-Cons with mouse controls , a 7.9-inch screen with HDR support, and a new C-button for online GameChat . The Switch 2 features five times as much storage as the original Switch, starting at 256GB, and is only compatible with MicroSD Express cards for storage upgrades.

The new system on its own starts at a price of $449.99 with bundles available for $499.99 . The Switch 2 also launched alongside a host of new accessories , including a new Pro controller and an official Nintendo Switch 2 camera.

We're only one year into the life of the Switch 2. Let's not get too ahead of ourselves by thinking about the next generation just yet. That said, it will be interesting to see whether Nintendo releases Switch 2 variants, like the upgraded Switch OLED and handheld-only Switch Lite that followed the original Switch.

Nintendo has yet to announce any sort of new hardware, so it's likely still a ways off. The company has plans to increase the price of the console in September 2026 , so even if we do get a Switch 2 Lite or Switch 2 OLED, it's likely to be much more expensive.

Noah Hunter is a freelance writer and reviewer with a passion for games and technology. He co-founded Final Weapon, an outlet focused on nonsense-free Japanese gaming (in 2019) and has contributed to various publishers writing about the medium.

articles.title: The End of Oak Street Is a Proud Product of the Spielberg '80s That's Fun to Be Around… Even If It Doesn’t Have the Same Bite as the Films That Inspired It
articles.summary: The End of Oak Street hits all the right nostalgic notes for a family adventure clearly inspired by the '80s most iconic sci fi films. David Robert Mitchell pulls from the same back of tricks that made It Follows a cult classic to add just enough plumage to the dinosaurs to make his film more than just a Spielberg impression.
articles.body:
The End of Oak Street is streaming on HBO Max now.

The End of Oak Street follows a family, led by Anne Hathaway and Ewan McGregor, as their neighborhood mysteriously teleports from an early ‘80s suburban landscape into the swampy age of dinosaurs, leaving them to fight for survival against a crew of beasts that look a little more like what passes for “scientifically accurate” these days. (They’ve got feathers and fur and everything.) It’s really a blank canvas of a science-fiction conceit. As specific as it may sound, “family must survive dinosaurs” can go a million different ways. It’s an engaging premise no matter which direction the filmmakers choose, but it’s also one that’s pretty familiar. The dangers lurking in the swamp of a family-forward dinosaur adventure are the impossible to avoid comparisons to Jurassic Park . That’s the bar The End of Oak Street, intentionally or not, fair or otherwise, has set for itself.

So, how does a dinosaur movie set itself apart from such obvious influences? The answer for The End of Oak Street seems to be, don’t. Instead, lean into them.

First, I have to say this movie might have been created in a lab just for me. I’m an ’80s kid, so the setting hits all the right heartstrings. I’m always here for a good, warmhearted adventure yarn, an energy the trailer for this film has piles of. On top of that, I love indie movies, and David Robert Mitchell, whose It Follows is a creepy experiment in creating eeriness, is making his first film in eight years and bringing dinosaurs along for as Spielbergian a ride as any you’ve seen in recent memory. These are all good things.

The End of Oak Street mostly delivers on all the expectations I had for this movie. By the time the dinosaurs show up, the movie turns into a fun little creature feature pretty quickly. The dinosaurs don’t look quite the way we’re used to seeing them on screen, which effectively modernizes them in a way Jurassic Park never really has. They can be scary and campy in equal measure. There’s a sequence that includes a memorably goofy photo op followed immediately by a harrowing escape. It’s a combination that works when the movie is in its stride.

But I say Oak Street mostly delivers because the film is walking a fine line where loving and effective homage is on the right and “I’ve just seen this before” is on the left. It’s those influences and those sleeves David Robert Mitchell is wearing them on. He clearly loves adventure films of the ‘80s, you can even hear it in the score from the production logos on. This film would have been right at home 40 years ago. But the audience isn’t mysteriously teleported to 40 years ago, and there are moments in the film that left me trying to outrun some outdated cheese.

For example, the film can be incredibly sweet and earnest. There’s an honest love for the setting, the ’80s in suburbia, that’s evident in every frame of the film’s first act. But that sweetness borders on saccharine at times, feeling like an affectation that’s not totally earned. In parts, it's a script that’s being read to me, admittedly with a lot of heart, but there’s a stiffness to it nonetheless.

Among all of that sticky sweetness, though, there are genuinely terrific moments, including one that I even found legitimately shocking. I would, were I a cooler person, describe my state in the aftermath of that scene as “shook.” But the key to all of the moments that worked is a decision David Robert Mitchell clearly made early in the development of The End of Oak Street – that no matter how many feathered dinosaurs appear on screen, this movie is about the family.

Putting a family dynamic front and center is a staple of all the Spielberg sci-fi Oak Street is borrowing from. Whether it’s the harsh light and wind blowing through the curtains calling up Close Encounters of the Third Kind or all the dinosaurs (and their poop) giving Jurassic Park in sometimes very literal, one-to-one ways, family dynamics are always the more important thing happening on screen. And so, while this is a movie about a wormhole blipping an entire neighborhood into dino-times, it’s really always about navigating difficult times in a marriage. And not only from the couple’s perspective, but the children’s as well.

That a wonky science-fiction trope leading to what could easily have been a spec script for Jurassic Park 8 that was rejected for being too weird is turned into a capable metaphor for a crumbling marriage is no small task. While the writer/director deserves the prehistoric flowers for pulling that off, I do think the bulk of the credit goes to Anne Hathaway. She’s having a pretty great year , and The End of Oak Street is coasting right along on that streak. As the mother of the pack, she’s strong and fiercely protective, but also frayed at the edges in all the right ways. She’s barely holding it together as the brutally realistic yin to Ewan McGregor’s relentlessly positive “it’s just all gonna be alright” yang. She’s grounded in a way that’s crucial to pulling off the metaphor-asaurus that David Robert Mitchell is aiming for.

Another thing that can’t be overlooked is the runtime. It’s about 90 minutes, and while this may be an unfair claim to make, I bet there’s a 105-minute version of this movie that just doesn’t work as well. An obvious thing that’s missing from that runtime is an explanation. And that is great. How the neighborhood actually transports somewhere else remains a mystery that the film never even thinks about unravelling. There’s some vague talk with some science-y words, and a touch of exposition from a radio broadcast heard from off-camera, but to incorporate more of an expertise or a character that could offer a definitive scientific explanation for the mysterious events, would’ve been a film-destroying mistake. Keeping the film to 90 minutes avoids that urge to explain stuff that does not need explaining, or over-complicating what is a straightforward survival tale to the detriment of what the movie is really about, which again, is about Anne Hathaway weathering a rough patch in what to everybody else appears to be the picture of happiness.

The other thing I really like about this movie is the visual set-up and payoff. One way David Robert Mitchell pulls this off is something my film nerd side is excited to talk about, which is the use of a split diopter lens. To get technical for a moment, a split diopter is an arrangement of glass on the lens that allows for two focal lengths in the same shot so that subjects in the very near foreground can be in focus while the background is in focus as well. But it’s not like everything is just in focus, there’s also a visible line in the frame separating the two subjects, so the audience’s attention is drawn to both in a much more distinct way.

Anyway, I love seeing split diopters because you don’t accidentally use them. They’re representative of a clear choice being made. Sometimes there’s just information on screen because we need to get from one scene to the next, but when you can tell a bag of tricks is being opened, I generally appreciate the effort. So where does a split diopter relate to the visual set-ups and payoffs in this movie? To me it seems the moments where the focus is split are when a character is hiding something. There are some uncomfortably framed split focus shots seen in the trailers, which take place during a tense and important moment for the family. They happen in a few other places as well, in spots where what’s being discussed in the foreground isn’t quite jiving with what’s happening in the background. Pay attention to which moments are framed at a distance as well. Instead of just a standard two-shot, there are conversations we see through a window, or over a hedge, or in the reflection of a mirror. This is a movie that’s undeniably thoughtful in its visuals.

There’s also some great, eerie blocking at play that sets up the world our characters start in to juxtapose the world they find themselves in later. This is something that David Robert Mitchell did really well in It Follows, and he excels at it again here in The End of Oak Street. The movie’s opening act is admittedly a little slow; in spite of the brisk 90-minute runtime, there’s a methodical pace to the stretch of film leading up to the first dinosaurs on screen. But what’s happening in those lingering shots of a treeline, the edits that feel a beat too slow after a character leaves frame… they’re all set-ups. Later in the film, those treelines that the film took great pains to establish as a safe part of ’80s suburbia are no longer empty, but instead are hiding something dangerous. Those edits that take an extra beat after the kids exit the shot suddenly feel like maybe we’re waiting to see something else show up.

The high-water mark for this technique is in a oner in the middle of the movie. The family is running away from a T. rex (a chunk of this shot is seen in the trailer) and it starts with near misses and ends with, as Dr. Malcolm said in The Lost World, running and screaming. The shot is a great little microcosm for what works about this movie. It’s also admittedly a little hokey, making it a microcosm of the things that don’t work about this movie as well.

But ultimately, the movie is like an old friend. There aren’t a lot of surprises, but you still enjoy their company. Maybe you haven’t seen each other in eight years or so, but there doesn’t need to be any explanation when you get back together. You know their secrets, warts and all, so maybe they don’t impress you like they used to but damn if it isn’t nice to see them again anyway. In spite of being a little under the influence of nostalgic sci-fi adventures, David Robert Mitchell and Anne Hathaway in particular add enough plumage to the familiar so that The End of Oak Street… finds a way.

articles.body:
There are numerous pets to collect to complete your index in Steal an Egg . Each pet appears in the various available biomes , and you'll need to consistently steal and hatch eggs from those regions to unlock them all. We'll be listing out all the pets in Steal an Egg with a checklist you can use to keep track of every one you've unlocked.

LATEST UPDATE: All New Pets Added in the Slick Rick Update

For the Slick Rick update , released on Nov. 14 , a new vendor has become available. Slick Rick has the chance to appear in the Alien Planet's lagoon at random times. Although Slick Rick does not sell eggs or pets, a new biome has become available called the Stormlands.

It's between the Prehistoric and Cosmic biomes, and is available to all players with at least 150m speed. There's also an exclusive series of pets you can hatch from the Storm Egg, which you can unlock by getting Thunderstones that fall during the Skyfall event. The Skyfall event happens every 30 minutes, on the hour and half-hour intervals.

Here's a list of all the eggs and pets that appear in the Stormlands.

These are the limited-time pets you can get from the Stormy Egg. Unlike other exclusive pets for limited eggs, the chances to acquire any of these pets is not listed.

There are eight pets for every biome in Steal an Egg. The larger and more exotic the egg that appears in the biome, the higher the likelihood you have of getting an animal that has a higher rarity or one with a unique mutation . All eggs reset every in-game night, which happens every four and a half minutes.

These are all of the pets you can get from each biome in Steal an Egg. Of these options, only the Brainrot Eggs cannot be obtained from a biome, as they are only available in the Store, and you have to use Robux to unlock them.

articles.title: The Best LEGO Harry Potter Sets for Fans of the Franchise
articles.summary: There are a lot of LEGO Harry Potter sets on the market. These are our top picks for the best picks in 2026.
articles.body:
LEGO Harry Potter faces a unique challenge, because the Warner Bros. media universe, upon which it is based, is limited – just eight core movies , the last of which debuted 15 years ago. The Fantastic Beasts films also take place in the Potter universe. But those films are divisive at best, and for the last one, Fantastic Beasts: The Secrets of Dumbledore , LEGO didn't create any corresponding LEGO sets – a first for what has been, to this point, a successful partnership.

But in 2024, the LEGO designers injected new life into the Potter franchise, embarking on their most ambitious multi-year project to date – a brand-new, fully realized recreation of Hogwarts Castle. LEGO is releasing the minifigure-scaled model piecemeal – one building at a time – beginning with the new Great Hall and Boathouse . Two years on, the castle is still a work in progress .

TL;DR: These Are the Best LEGO Harry Potter Sets in 2026

LEGO Hogsmeade Village – Collectors' Edition

LEGO Sorcerer’s Stone – Collectors’ Edition

We've updated our LEGO Harry Potter guide to include all the main LEGO sets you need to build the main castle as well as our other favorites from the franchise. Here are the best sets available as of November 2026, each of which makes a great gift for Harry Potter fans .

The third classroom set of its kind, Herbology Class takes place in one of Hogwarts' greenhouses. It's captures the events of Chamber of Secrets, specifically when the students are learning how to repot Mandrake plants. The set comes with three minifigures of Hermione, Neville, and Professor Sprout.

The Main Tower set is over two feet tall, which really lends some perspective on how big this eventual castle model is going be. It looks great on the outside, but the interior really places this set a cut above the rest. You get the moving staircases in the actual tower. And in the building off to the side, you get the Gryffindor common room and the trials for the Sorcerer's Stone. We built and photographed this set for its launch.

We reviewed the Hogwarts Castle and Grounds set when it first came out and were thoroughly impressed. You could buy a bigger, 5500+-piece LEGO Hogwarts Castle with several fully realized interiors. But this smaller, prettier build will suit most Potter fans for a fraction of the price. While it isn't part of the LEGO Architecture line , it's defintely worth building and displaying in the same way.

This microfigure-scaled depiction of Diagon Alley pairs well with the Hogwarts Castle and Grounds we feature above, and it is of similar scale, detail, and scope. The buildings include Weasleys' Wizard Wheezes, Florean Fortescue’s Ice Cream Parlor, Ollivanders, Mr. Mulpepper’s Apothecary, Gringotts Wizarding Bank, the Leaky Cauldron, and The Daily Prophet. The set also comes with 12 microfigures, including the classic trio. The entire set folds in – which creates a more realistic depiction of a crowded London street – and folds out to make it displayable.

Unlike Diagon Alley, which is an enchanted street hidden in the heart of London, Hogsmeade is a dedicated, all-wizarding village, which Harry and his friends visit for the first time in Prisoner of Azkaban . This set includes seven buildings, scaled to the size of the now-retired Diagon Alley set: Honeydukes, Owl Post, The Three Broomsticks, Dervish and Banges, Scrivenshaft's Quill Shop, Zonko’s Joke Shop, and Hog’s Head.

This is the most recent chunk of the massive modular Hogwarts Castle, currently in progress. Madame Pomfrey's Hospital Wing deals with all sorts of magical medical maladies. But in addition to the hospital wing itself, the set also includes the Defense Against the Dark Arts classroom (from the third year, when Lupin taught the class) and the Ravenclaw common room.

To see our entire Hogwarts Castle build, currently in progress, you can check it out here .

Celebrating 25 years since the launch of the first Potter film, this set features a massive Hedwig, perched atop various Hogwarts iconography, including the Sorcerer's Stone, Harry's trunk, a spell book, and a Gryffindor notebook. There's lots of secrets; turn the dials, and the owl and chess piece move. There are also microscale dioramas hidden throughout the build, including the troll scene, the Sorcerer's Stone trials, and the Hogwarts Express at Platform 9 3/4.

An essential component to the massive, minifigure-scaled Hogwarts Castle, the East Wing includes the Slytherin Common Room and the Chamber of Secrets. The latter connects to Moaning Myrtle's bathroom above it and features a giant Salazar Slytherin head. The East Wing also includes a bridge and a walkway, which connect to the Great Hall and Main Tower sets, respectively.

You can find our build of the entire Hogwarts Castle here .

This build of the Hogwarts Crest stands out, thanks to the color contrast between its four houses. Beneath the crest is a scroll with the school's motto: "Draco Dormiens Nunquam Titillandus," which translated from Latin means, "Never tickle a sleeping dragon." The crest also contains secret compartments that house the four founders' relics: Godric Gryffindor's Sword, Helga Hufflepuff's Cup, Rowena Ravenclaw's Diadem, and Salazar Slytherin's Locket.

The smallest LEGO version of Hogwarts Castle has a lot of character to it, capturing all its iconic structures: the Great Hall, the Main Tower, the East Wing, the Viaduct, and lastly, the Astronomy Tower, looming over it all. It includes some Easter eggs, including a Chamber of Secrets hidden underneath the East Wing. And it is a bargain by LEGO standards, costing $40 for 700 pieces.

How Many Harry Potter LEGO Sets Are There?

As of November 2026, 35 Harry Potter sets are available at the LEGO store, capturing moments and locations from across the entire movie franchise.

What's the future for LEGO Harry Potter?

In 2027, Harry Potter will reboot on HBO—not as new films, but as a long-running television series . And at that point, LEGO might correspondingly reboot the entire LEGO line to match a new aesthetic.

Harry Potter is still incredibly popular, even if it's not as much of a cultural phenomenon as it was in its heyday; nowadays, it's more of an institution.

And of course, there's the inevitable backlash – some of it the naturally-occurring type when something becomes this popular – and some of it self-wrought, by the author's rhetoric. Where you fall on that debate , and whether you separate art from the artist, is a personal decision. But if you do, there's a lot of LEGO sets that you might want to check out. And now, you know what they are.

articles.summary: These are the 10 most valuable cards in Magic: The Gathering’s Star Trek set, led by Captain Jean-Luc Picard’s $300 Showcase card, Mr. Spock, and Captain Kirk.
articles.body:
Magic: The Gathering’s Star Trek set has been hotly anticipated or controversial, depending on where you stand on the topic of Universes Beyond, but there’s no denying Wizards of the Coast is going all out for it.

Mr. Spock, Science Officer (Borderless) (Surge Foil)

With four Commander decks, a Secret Lair drop, and plenty more, there’s a whole bunch for Trekkies to collect. Still, if you’re cracking Collector Boosters (or get really, really lucky with a Play Booster), you may find some of the most valuable cards in the set. Which cards are most valuable? We’ve listed the top 10 below for you.

As ever, pre-release pricing will shift considerably. We’ll be sure to update this list in the coming days once TCGplayer’s data is updated.

The Most Valuable Star Trek Cards In Magic’s Latest Set

Showcase lands are a recurring theme in this list, and this one starts us off at $60.

A Mountain/Plains, the Sacred Foundry taps for red or white mana.

Up next is the cube-shaped vessel of the Borg. It’s an artifact spacecraft with affinity for artifact creatures, and feeds into the assimilate mechanic, which lets you grab something and turn it into a Borg.

This Showcase Borg Cube variant will set you back $80 at the time of writing.

Another land on our list, this Swamp/Forest taps for black or green mana and will set you back around $81 right now.

A card with an awful lot of text on it, Q, Stacking the Deck lets you exile cards from the top of your library to exile a nonland card, which in turn lets you create a copy of a card in your hand.

I’m still trying to get my head around it, but the Showcase version is $85 at the time of writing.

Another land, Breeding Pool, was seen in Edge of Eternities last year. This Forest Island taps for green or blue mana, and the Showcase version is $92 .

This Legendary crea…. Wait. No, this is a Mountain, just a basic Mountain.

The Surge Foil Mountain , to be precise, is currently selling for over $90. Expect to see this one slide soon, unless I’m missing something.

Looking for a fun Commander for Saga cards? You’ve found one with Dathon, His Heart Open.

Casting an enchantment draws you a card, while Sagas deal two damage to each opponent, plus you can run up the counters on your enchantments - a little like the Counter Blitz precon.

The Showcase version here is $100 at the time of writing.

Whether you’re a Kirk or Picard fan, you’re well catered for with this set. Captain James T. Kirk’s Showcase card is going for around $170 ahead of launch weekend.

When it enters or attacks, you can choose one of three options, or go bigger if you have no cards in hand.

2 - Mr. Spock, Science Officer (Borderless) (Surge Foil)

A mono-blue creature that nets players double card advantage was always going to be a big draw (get it?) for players, but adding the inimitable Leonard Nimoy has meant Mr. Spock, Science Officer’s borderless , surge foil version is sitting at around $200.

The late, great Patrick Stewart was always going to be on this list somewhere, and the Showcase version of Captain Jean-Luc Picard is sitting at $300, making it the most valuable card in the set.

Picard’s card (heh) gives other creatures +1/+1, and casting a creature or spacecraft gets you a 1/1 Officer token. Get seven of those, and you can search your library for a spacecraft and put it on the battlefield with seven charge counters.

articles.title: The Magic: The Gathering Animated Series, Planeswalker, Is Finally Coming to Netflix in 2027
articles.summary: Wizards of the Coast and Netflix have revealed their long-in-development Magic: The Gathering series is called Planeswalker, and it's coming sometime in 2027.
articles.body:
There's been a Magic: The Gathering animated series cooking in the background since 2019, and now at MagicCon Atlanta, Wizards of the Coast has revealed that it's called Planeswalker, and it's coming sometime in 2027.

Rather than being some epic live-action fantasy show like Game of Thrones, Netflix is taking the same approach it did with Castlevania and making Planeswalker an animated series. But making a show in a universe as expansive as Magic: The Gathering is challenging, due to the nearly infinite worlds it encompasses. It sounds like the show isn't shying away from that.

The show will be centered on Planeswalker Chandra Nalaar. According to a synopsis shared with IGN, she's "a volatile pyromancer hunted for her gifts, and haunted by her past. Confronted by an insidious force, Chandra and some of the most legendary Planeswalkers must harness their extraordinary abilities, navigate treacherous alliances, and battle their own inner demons to prevent a cataclysmic war that threatens to consume their very existence. As the line between victory and annihilation grows thinner, a single spark determines the fate of thousands of worlds."

Every great story begins with a spark. Here’s your first look at PLANESWALKER, a new animated series based on Magic: The Gathering. Coming to Netflix in 2027. — Netflix (@netflix) November 13, 2026

Every great story begins with a spark. Here’s your first look at PLANESWALKER, a new animated series based on Magic: The Gathering. Coming to Netflix in 2027.

Chandra was also the character that appeared in the first teaser for the show years ago, so it looks like this is still the same thing. However, when Netflix first announced that it'd be working on a Magic: The Gathering series back in 2019, it had Avengers: Endgame directors Joe and Anthony Russo running the show . The Russo Brothers left back in 2021 , and in the five years since then, ownership of the show has passed to Terry Matalas, who will be running it alongside Cindy Appel.

Matalas previously served as the showrunner for VisionQuest, which just ended and was well received. In the IGN review, we gave the premiere a 7, and reviewer Jesse Schedeen said, "VisionQuest may struggle a bit to reestablish the titular hero in this post-WandaVision MCU, but at least the series has James Spader’s Ultron to fall back upon."

MagicCon Atlanta Preview Panel – Screenshots

Magic: The Gathering has a ton of lore to build a show off of, and it's going to be interesting to see how it handles a multiverse that'd put Marvel to shame. At least we won't have to wait too long before it debuts in 2027. Let's just hope Netflix doesn't wait until November to put it out.

articles.title: The Biggest Crime in Apple TV's Heist Thriller 12 12 12 Is Its Botched Premise
articles.summary: Apple TV’s new heist series 12 12 12 is predicated on a timeline-hopping gimmick that only works as an elevator pitch.
articles.body:
This is a spoiler-free review of the first two episodes of 12 12 12 , streaming on Apple TV now.

Apple TV’s 12 12 12 operates under these invented cardinal rules of a professional heist: It takes 12 months to plan, 12 hours to execute, and if the cops don’t catch the perpetrators in 12 days, they never will. (Why this didn’t premiere on December 12, I’ll never understand.) The series rests its entire weight on this premise, hopping between the three phases of a heist organized by Jamie Dornan’s Paul Galvin, a retired thief pulled back in for one last job, and the FBI agent relentlessly on his trail, Anthony Mackie’s Jack Strickland. The question is, then, does 12 12 12’s gimmick work? Based on the first two episodes, “I’m robbing the house on Christmas Eve while the family’s at mass” and “I Want My Halo Back,” the answer seems to be: not really.

12 12 12 starts with eyebrow-raising intrigue, as a crumpled, naked man slithers out of a lockbox inside a fancy-looking bank vault and starts cracking open safes. But the cutaway from this scene — right into the 12 12 12 explanation — is only the first instance of the main problem with the show thus far: switching over to a new window of time kills any of the momentum the previous scenes had going for them. 12 12 12 also approaches each of its nonlinear storylines with the same level of urgency. Hour 1 of Paul’s heist to steal the equivalent of one billion physical U.S. dollars — which, just how bulky is that in comparison, say, to the Breaking Bad storage unit stack ? — from a Swiss bank moves with practically the same verve as Jack getting wise to what’s happened on the Day 1 hunt. It doesn’t help with differentiating either when both characters keep referencing “what happened in Newark” as the murky botched job from the past they won’t shut the hell up about nor actually explain beyond the obvious trauma they incurred from it.

12 12 12’s first two episodes, written by Dudi Appleton and Jim Keebble, treat that concept as though it’s so complicated that the audience could only follow the plot by spoon-feeding us time and place, and the script doubles down on this. The plot itself is full of cliches so that when it posits an occasionally unique idea it, by comparison, feels nearly revelatory. Of course, it often squanders that goodwill just as quickly. Just when you think 12 12 12 is going somewhere, its timeline triptych appears and swipes over to a new time period, resetting the action and deflating any of the excitement the show had just built. The dialogue is full of insufferable back-and-forths that are either inane or could have come from nearly any primetime cable procedural that’s attempting a quippy Marvel-ized punch-up.

Mackie and Dornan, two very competent actors, both make great efforts to do what they can with the trite material but to little avail. There’s only so much even accomplished actors can do with lines like “What if the only thing I’m good at is being a thief?” as Paul contemplates his girlfriend’s surprise pregnancy, or “You stole from me, Galvin. Now you’re gonna know how it feels,” as Jack promises to get revenge on Paul. For a show about pulling off the biggest bank heist in European history, it’s botched the job.

articles.title: Magic: The Gathering’s Star Trek Commander Precons Ranked: Why We Are the Borg Takes the Top Spot
articles.summary: We ranked all four Magic: The Gathering Star Trek Commander precons—from Picard’s Federation Fleet to We Are the Borg—by gameplay, value, and key reprints.
articles.body:
Magic: The Gathering’s Star Trek set is finally here, closing out a particularly packed release schedule for Wizards of the Coast’s long-running TCG.

Star Trek is the seventh set of the year, and it brings with it another four Commander decks to take this year’s total to 17. Still, as we all know, not all decks are created equal - so which one comes out on top?

The Klingons or the Borg? Picard or Spock? Here’s our ranking.

If you’re picking up all four decks because you’re a Trekkie, or you just love new precons, Amazon has cut the price of the bundle again to just $224.97 , basically offsetting the “Universes Beyond” tax.

That’s not the Collector Editions, though: Those are well over $100 each. They include the same cards, but all in foil.

Magic: The Gathering | Star Trek Commander Deck Bundle

Magic: The Gathering | Star Trek Commander Deck - Federation Fleet

Color Identity: Jeskai (blue, red, white)

Magic loves to put heroic precons in Jeskai colors, and Federation Fleet is no exception - although it does come last in our ranking.

Its primary Commander, Jean-Luc Picard, Luminary, is a four-cost 2/4 that draws you cards as you play historic permanents, which then triggers the Seek Out mechanic. This lets you charge up a Spacecraft and add a counter to another target creature.

It’s not that it’s not a fun, cohesive deck, but it’s definitely just not as interesting on a mechanical level as the others in this set.

Magic: The Gathering | Star Trek Commander Deck - Klingon Fury

Color Identity: Mardu (white, black, red)

Reprints of note: Sword of Light, Shadow and World at War

Worf, Defiant Commander is in charge of the Klingon Fury deck, which makes use of the Battlefront mechanic to encourage players to play aggressively.

Worf creates Klingon Warrior tokens when it hits the battlefield, and the more opponents you attack on your turn, the more cards you exile from the top of your library, which you can play until the end of your next turn.

It’s not quite cheating big creatures into play, but it should mean you’re well-stocked with options as long as you keep Worf around.

Magic: The Gathering | Star Trek Commander Deck - Landing Party

Color Identity: Bant (green, white, blue)

Reprints of note: Ancient Greenwarden, Scute Swarm, Exploration, Heroic Intervention

Commander Spock is the logical choice for a Commander in Bant colors, and Wizards of the Coast has made it so here (sorry).

Landing Party’s Strange New Worlds mechanic helps play cards more quickly if you’ve got more differently named lands in the set. Given there are 40 in the deck, that should be easily done, but this deck also gives you a big bundle of non-basic lands in Bant colors if you need them.

Captain Kirk, Boldly Going, is another Commander option. William Shatner himself is a 3/4 with vigilance who powers up your Spacecraft cards. The card can also grab you land cards or the Enterprise from your library or graveyard.

Magic: The Gathering | Star Trek Commander Deck - We are the Borg

Color Identity: Esper (white, blue, black)

Reprints of note: Toxic Deluge, Unwinding Clock, Morphic Pool

Our top pick for the Commander precons in the Star Trek set is We Are The Borg . Standing somewhere between artifact synergies and a “what’s yours is mine” deck, The Borg Queen pumps artifact creatures and also assimilates cards to your side of the battlefield.

Unwinding Clock is a very welcome reprint here since it fits nicely into just about any other artifact strategy, and Locutus of Borg can help you pull even more Borg to the table. It’s a deck that’s likely to get out of hand pretty quickly, and for that reason, it’s our top pick.

articles.title: Leave None Alive - Phantom Blade Zero Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Leave None Alive is a Tale side quest in Phantom Blade Zero, which begins in the Village of Lu.
articles.body:
Leave None Alive is a Tale side quest in Phantom Blade Zero , which begins in the Village of Lu.

It can be started upon talking to Old Man Gen in his hut at the start of the area.

Return to the Weeping Creek Valley Outpost and the Crimson Forest Thieves' Camp

Return to the Weeping Creek Valley Outpost to find almost everyone here has become an enemy you need to defeat. Here you can defeat a monk who drops the Prayer Beads, a key story item for this quest and necessary to obtain an item later in the area.

After this, teleport to the Thieves' Camp in the Crimson Forest to find the same thing. Defeating the enemies here will drop the Thief's Manual, another key item needed for this quest.

Progress through the Village of Lu until you reach the fight against Master Bi Hai of Kuye Temple . Before the fight starts, Soul will talk to a thief by the door who will mention th events at the Thieves' Camp in the Crimson Forest. The Thief's Manual you found can be handed over by choosing "Thief's relics".

Doing so will complete theis stage of the quest and also give you the Arrowward accessory.

Tell The Monk You "Do Not Believe" at the Survivors' Courtyard

Progress all the way through the outside of the Village of Lu until you free the third body and open the well. After exiting the building, take the zipline and jump down.

You will find several enemies attacking a door. Defeat them and then interact to free the villagers behind the door.

In the corner you can find a Monk. Talk to him and he will ask if you believe or not. You MUST tell him that you "Do Not Believe" in order to progress this quest.

Upon doing this, you can hand the Prayer Beads over to the Monk. In return he will give you the Agarwood Prayer Beads, an accessory which reduces recovery time by 15% after your guard is broken.

articles.title: PS5 QSSR Updates Revealed for Marvel's Spider-Man 2, Arc Raiders, and More
articles.summary: Sony has confirmed Marvel's Spider-Man 2, Arc Raiders, and four more games are receiving QSSR support on base PS5s.
articles.body:
Sony has confirmed Marvel's Spider-Man 2 , Arc Raiders , and four more games are receiving QSSR support on base PS5s.

The list of six newcomers joining the small-but-growing group of supported games was unveiled in a PlayStation.Blog post . In addition to confirmation that incoming updates will add QSSR (Quick Spectral Super Resolution), the post included testimonials from each of the studios' developers, who shared how the tech will impact visuals.

When Sony pulled back the curtain on QSSR in October, it came with confirmation that it had already been implemented in Marvel's Wolverine and Ghost of Yōtei. Now, we know that Insomniac's Marvel's Spider-Man 2, Remedy Entertainment's Control Resonant , Embark Studios' Arc Raiders and The Finals , Hello Games' No Man's Sky , and Expression Games' Hell Let Loose: Vietnam will soon take advantage of the AI upscaling tech.

In the case of Marvel's Spider-Man 2, QSSR is available as part of a new update that's out now.

"Having seen great results integrating QSSR in Marvel’s Wolverine, our team decided to bring it to Marvel’s Spider-Man 2 as well, in an update that’s live now!" Insomniac head of technology Mike Fitzgerald said. "We’re excited for players to swing back into our 2023 title and see QSSR’s exciting image stability and sharpness benefits in both Fidelity and Performance modes."

Remedy said QSSR will bring noticeable improvements in image stability and fine detail when it launches in a new update in December. Hello Games founder Sean Murray, meanwhile, promised that players can look forward to No Man's Sky looking "sharper, cleaner, and more beautiful" at the "best possible framerate" in the next few weeks. When exactly The Finals, Arc Raiders, and Hell Let Loose: Vietnam will receive their updates has yet to be announced.

PS5 Digital Console 30th Anniversary Limited Edition

"With the new QSSR coming soon to ARC Raiders and The Finals, we can deliver increased sharpness, better environmental clarity, and overall visual improvements to even more PlayStation players," Embark said. "We are very happy to see Sony’s continued investment in PlayStation technology translate into meaningful improvements for all players, bringing more immersive experiences across the PlayStation ecosystem."

Sony then teased that developers interested in using QSSR are "just getting started." More PS5 games are set to receive similar updates in the coming months, though which titles will join the list remains to be seen.

articles.title: Blade Runner 2099 Executive Producers Confirm Franchise Owners Are in Talks for AAA Video Game Adaptation
articles.summary: Andrew Kosove and Broderick Johnson, executive producers for Blade Runner 2099 and co-CEOs of Alcon Entertainment, have confirmed that they are in discussions to create a AAA video game based on the iconic cyberpunk franchise.
articles.body:
Andrew Kosove and Broderick Johnson, executive producers for Blade Runner 2099 and co-CEOs of Alcon Entertainment, the owner of the Blade Runner franchise, have confirmed that they are in discussions to create a AAA video game based on the iconic cyberpunk IP.

I got the chance to chat with Kosove and Johnson ahead of Blade Runner 2099’s release on Prime Video later this month. During our conversation, I brought up the wildly successful Cyberpunk 2077 , wondering why Blade Runner hasn’t had a similar AAA game made after it and if any conversations have been had about finally giving this IP a major modern video game release.

“Yes,” Kosove confirmed, and emphasized the phrase “AAA,” making it clear that Alcon has a grand vision for Blade Runner’s future in the gaming space. Of course, he couldn’t tell me much more, but impressed upon the importance of allowing players to “interact” with the world of Blade Runner in this hypothetical game.

This is big news for fans of Blade Runner and the cyberpunk genre, in general. While Blade Runner has enjoyed its status as a cult-classic and cornerstone of modern science fiction, it hasn’t exactly been blessed in the game department.

Based on IGN’s own list of Blade Runner games , the franchise has four licensed titles. The first, published in 1985 by CRL Group PLC for the Commodore 64, is an absolute dinosaur of a game that wasn’t well-received even at the time of its release. In the game, players hunt down replicants (here, replidroids) for bounty money. Due to the cost of movie rights at the time, this game was said to merely be “inspired” by the "Vangelis soundtrack" of Ridley Scott’s 1982 film and not a direct adaptation.

The next Blade Runner game, which was released in 1997, enjoyed far more critical acclaim and is still considered a classic to this day. Developed by Westwood Studios and published by Virgin Interactive, this point-and-click adventure title was one of the very first titles to use 3D character models and real-time environments. A remake was released in 2022.

Another game, titled Blade Runner 2033: Labyrinth, was announced in 2023 and developed by Annapurna Interactive. Unfortunately, the project is now largely considered to be canceled, having been delisted from Steam and removed from Annapurna’s website. (Blade Runner 2049: Replicant Pursuit was released in 2017. It was a short, tie-in VR experience meant to promote the second film, but not a full, official game.)

Given that it’s been nearly 30 years since Blade Runner fans have had a fresh, critically acclaimed video game adaptation, this latest news is extremely exciting and opens up an entire world of possibilities. And considering Kosove’s focus on player interactivity and AAA quality, it sounds like Alcon has a clear vision for what it wants this game to be — and I can’t wait to see what they come up with.

Blade Runner 2099 releases on Prime Video on November 25.

Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze .

articles.title: Secrets At the Heart of the Lake - Firefly's Memory Flowers Locations - Phantom Blade Zero Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Secrets at the Heart of the Lake is an optional Purple Story Quest in Phantom Blade Zero's Village of Lu. It can be started by picking up a memory flower
articles.body:
Secrets at the Heart of the Lake is an optional Purple Story Quest in Phantom Blade Zero 's Village of Lu. It can be started by picking up a memory flower from Firefly next to Zhuo Bi, the Gatekeeper , the first boss in the village.

Just to the left of his arena, you can find the flower.

There are five additional Memory Flowers you need to find in the Village of Lu. Most are located in the south-eastern corner of the village.

From the well, drop into the river next to you over the small bridge on your right. At the back, you can find the flower.

Head back up to the well and right to the Temple of Blue Fireflies. In the temple next to the bell with the mist barrier, you can find the flower.

Follow the main path until you reach the Dread Axe chained gate. Just to the right at a small shrine is the Memory Flower.

Upon crossing the walkway after removing the red-thread barrier, follow the path until you can fork right. A large lady enemy will be blocking the doorway to a house. Defeat her and go down the ladder found inside the house. A hole in the wall will lead outside, where you'll find the next Memory Flower on the ridge.

After you free the final soul and open the well, head outside and follow the dirt path over the tree. You'll see the next Memory Flower slightly to your right at the end of the path.

articles.title: After Another Year of Price Hikes, What Streaming Deals Will We Get for Black Friday 2026?
articles.body:
We’re officially in the thick of deals season, and if there’s one thing I personally spend way too much money on, it’s streaming subscriptions. It doesn't help that everyone keeps hiking prices, and deals are rarer than ever.

Thankfully, there’s one time of year where you can often get a decent amount of those very subscriptions for much cheaper than usual: Black Friday .

Almost every service is likely to drop some type of deal, though the majority will be on ad-supported plans. If you’ve been intrigued by any particular service, or want to strategize some free trials and cancellations, here’s what streaming deals I expect we’ll see for Black Friday this year.

In general, deals will certainly be live from Black Friday (November 27) to Cyber Monday (November 30). However, some services may launch their Black Friday deals in the week before the main event.

Starting from the top, obviously Amazon will be all over Black Friday (check out the retailer’s full sale schedule). Prime Video is included in Amazon memberships, which pretty much never go on sale. The service does offer a 30-day free trial and a hefty 50% discount for anyone under the age of 25.

Channel Add-Ons, however, like AMC+ and Britbox, will likely have deals through Prime Video in addition to their own platforms. Amazon’s general Black Friday sale starts November 19, but I imagine most Add-On discounts will appear on Black Friday proper.

Disney+ has always launched some sort of Black Friday deal, but as we’ve seen across streaming, the discounts have gotten less generous over time.

Last year , Black Friday came right after Disney+ rolled out a price hike. The Black Friday deal only applied to the ad-supported bundle of both services, dropping the monthly price from $12.99 to $4.99 for a full 12 months.

Disney+ increased prices again back in September , but the Hulu bundle actually stayed at $12.99. I’d guess we see the return of the $4.99 deal on the ad-supported bundle for a full 12-month window, but there’s a chance it only goes down to $5.99 to align with the new Disney+ pricing.

HBO Max is in a particularly weird place. Paramount finalized its acquisition of Warner Bros. earlier this year, and indicated early on in negotiations they were planning to merge their streaming services . More recently, Paramount announced that HBO Max and Paramount+ will be getting a new streaming bundle in early 2027 , which is likely a first step on the path to a full merger.

However, that doesn’t mean Black Friday deals are off the table. Last year , HBO Max offered a particularly generous deal, dropping the ad-supported plan to just $2.99/month for a 12-month period. We’ll likely see the same deal return this year, though potentially limited to six or even two months as HBO Max navigates a more uncertain future.

Paramount+ is in a similar boat to HBO Max, but I’m a bit more confident in this one, largely because Paramount+ has offered relatively consistent deals even as other services have shied away from them. Right now, for example, you can get 50% off an annual subscription using a promo code .

For Black Friday, Paramount+ will likely offer a two-month subscription deal on both of its ad-supported and ad-free Showtime plans. Yep, we might actually have an ad-free deal on our hands. In 2025 , Paramount+ dropped the prices of both subscriptions to $2.99/month, and given the consistency of deals since then, I expect to see the same deal return for 2026.

Speaking of ad-free, praise be Apple TV. Apple’s streaming service keeps it simple with one ad-free subscription plan, so if you’re dead set on picking up a new service without ads, this is your best bet.

Last year , Apple TV dropped the price of its subscription from $12.99 to $5.99/month for a six-month period. Since then, however, the service hiked prices by $2 for a standard monthly rate of $14.99. With that in mind, I expect to see the return of at least a six-month deal period, but the discount might be closer to $6.99 to hit the same discount percentage.

Peacock was actually one of the only streaming services that didn’t offer any Black Friday deal in 2025. That doesn’t mean we’re out of luck this year, but it isn’t a great sign, especially given the service just hiked prices again this Summer.

If you desperately want to catch up on Peacock’s sitcoms and reality TV lineup, I recommend keeping an eye out for deals on Walmart+ subscriptions . This is basically Walmart’s version of Amazon Prime, but it also includes Peacock Premium , and often get 50% discounts during major sales events.
