articles.title: When GTA 5 Took On Zuckerberg and Hit Peak Satire
articles.summary: This is how Rockstar brought together bad fashion, a miserable gangster, an exploding phone, and fake Zuckerberg getting his just deserts to create GTA 5's memorable takedown of Silicon Valley.
articles.body:
There’s a lot of shooting and driving in Grand Theft Auto missions, they’re kind of your main verbs in the game. You drive, shoot, and drive some more with the possibility of shooting again. They’re not very dynamic as a wireframe, so it’s a good thing that Rockstar leads the industry in storytelling, character, and satire.

Missions burst with thematic meaning, every second an opportunity to push someone forward or revel in gags. It doesn’t really matter what you do. In GTA, a mission that largely consists of buying cargo shorts against your will can rival casino heists, mid-air hijackings, and all-out urban warfare.

Friend Request is an early storyline mission in Grand Theft Auto V. Tutorials are behind us but Trevor has yet to join the team. Retired crook Michael De Santa is in deep trouble, so he turns to his old accomplice Lester for help. The free-as-in-speech-not-as-in-beer software enthusiast seems willing to set up a new job, but first he needs Michael to blow open the walled garden that is Jay Norris’s skull.

The CEO of LifeInvader, a clear stand-in for Facebook, is about to unveil his new surveillance nightmare: a prototype smartphone designed to “dock” with every single aspect of your existence. It’s one intrusion too far for a reclusive crank like Lester, so he tasks us with sabotaging it in a mission so linear it makes Marvel’s Wolverine look like Morrowind.

Not a whole lot! Many GTA missions stray from the shoot-em-up template, exploring the mundanity of the contemporary life that Rockstar aims to emulate. Some of our fondest GTA memories involve doing yoga and winning danceoffs, but Friend Request is uneventful even by those standards. Your first task is to go shopping, swinging by the ersatz Urban Outfitters for some techy threads.

Rockstar’s reputation for railroaded, handholdy missions is notorious and not entirely unearned, and here it’s at its most egregious. During the short trip to SubUrban, Michael is free to shoot guns and cause trouble despite the hefty Jansport slung jauntily over his shoulder. You’ll have to lose your wanted level to continue, which is reasonable enough.

Your options dwindle as soon as you enter the store. You must buy a vest and shorts. Choose a festive Aloha shirt or a comfy flannel and the shopkeeper will bar your progression and roast you with a frankly unwarranted “what are those?”

Once you’re in disguise, you can equip guns but can’t fire them without triggering a failure state. You can approach the LifeInvader office, but the front door won’t open, and trying to blow your way in will force a restart. Drop a sticky bomb and its fission mailed before it even hits the ground.

You have to pose as an IT temp, share a cig with this guy Rickie, and follow the overpaid programmer through the open plan office. You’ve now lost the ability to sprint, and besides an unlocked basement, all of the conference rooms with cutesy names are inaccessible. You can only observe until it’s time to close some pop-ups.

This is probably the most “gameplay” in Friend Request, if you consider clicking to be ludologically satisfying, and even here you’re limited. You can’t click any of the websites, not that you’d want to, you sicko, nor can you open any of the enticing folders and hard drives that are just sitting on the desktop begging to be file-explored.

Once you clean up Rickie's infested computer you can access the LifeInvader phone prototype in an unguarded room. There’s no need to be sneaky, no one can see you and there’s literally nothing you can do to draw their attention as you fit the device with a miniature explosive. Once the job is done, you have no option but to politely leave. You can’t play the arcade games, avail yourself of productivity-enhancing snacks, or even follow this guy into his job interview. He’ll just wait there, clutching his resume, “#OpenToWork” eternally circling his LinkedIn profile years before the green frame of shame was invented.

Time to go home. You still can’t shoot, though you can use your fists and engage in enough vehicular carnage to earn a police response. Once you arrive, you must kick Tracey off the couch and tune in to Jay Norris, live from the Vinewood Bowl.

While the wunderkind tech giant preaches to a choir of sycophantic fans, Michael places a call to the sabotaged smartphone and blasts Norris’s head off. You can choose not to hit send, but if you miss the mark the event is over in seconds and you fail the mission. There isn’t even any amusing dillydallying in the scene to reward your curiosity. Either hit the mission complete button or don’t. Do it in eight and a half minutes for a gold medal.

On paper, it’s the opposite of exciting. You go shopping and go to work. It’s not hard to imagine how Agent 47 would have handled the whole ordeal, infiltrating the glass-walled workplace and inserting himself into all kinds of startup office drama amidst a clockwork Hitman level. The end result would have been the same though, so maybe it wouldn’t have mattered how we got there. The important stuff is what you see on the way.

Within the sandbox of GTA’s open worlds are palaces purpose-built for spectacular cinematic setpieces. A suspiciously detailed museum, or a motel with chest-high walls, maybe. Busy seaports and concrete canals. These bespoke and intentional spaces exist to demonstrate Rockstar’s technical mastery and excellence in encounter design. The folks in Edinburgh like to flex their muscles, and a mission like Friend Request is just a different way of showing off.

It’s the signature satirical moment of GTA 5, a provocative piss-take ripped from the headlines as well as from the third-best Gerard Butler movie. Friend Request is a showcase for Rockstar’s edgy bravado packed into a bite-sized breather mission with more jokes-per-minute than a whole season of 30 Rock.

If Rockstar’s railroading has an upside, it’s making sure the stuff they’re forcing you to see is highly-concentrated entertainment in bulk. With our hand fully in the designer’s grasp, we’re led through a slice of life diorama dense with gags and observations, like an EPCOT exhibit that transports us to the early 2010s.

It was a time of economic exuberance, when a couple of` guys with a crazy dream could open a restaurant where appetizers are called “shareables.” Tech startups emerged aggressively as the iPhone revolution took hold, with low interest rates enabling lavish offsites and office perks like matcha on tap and unlimited fig bars. LifeInvader’s workplace obsession with air guitar echoes entire Agile squads doing the Harlem Shake, all for the Vine.

Friend Request captures this earnest arrogance with a field researcher’s eye, no doubt informed by the observations of Rockstar creatives throughout their global network of office spaces where they spent a lot of time. Whiteboards are plastered with mission statements and sprint roadmaps, while the workers in conformist techvests and khakis engage in mindless chatter and awkward standup meetings. It’s a cathartic experience for anyone who’s ever had to book a pod via a glitchy tablet or wait for the water cooler to complete a firmware update. We didn’t know how good we had it.

Any “modern” satire risks aging immediately upon release. Games take a long time to make, and the targets of their pointed barbs might be old news by the time anyone gets to play them, forgotten like Foursquare and Klout. The tech industry is different now.

It traded bright and beachy millennial optimism for apocalyptic AI-pilled doom, with cold-pressed kombucha replaced by nicotine pouches and black market peptides. The Jay Norris of our current hellscape wouldn’t be wearing a “gillet,” whatever that is, but instead rocking a dainty chain and a $3,000 t-shirt that’s too big. His rhetoric, however, probably wouldn’t change all that much.

American culture has been stuck in a rut for a while. You could travel back in time to 2013 wearing exactly what you are now and no one would bat an eye, though they probably won’t believe your warning about the Costco Guys. The memes might be different and the pivot to video is vertical, but otherwise we’re still very much living in the surveillance economy Friend Request predicted, our anxieties around social media and privacy exacerbated even more by glasses that record our every move and ugly pendants that are always listening.

Rockstar’s world is no longer the one outside your window, but it’s illustrative of how we got here. Its problems seem quaint in comparison, when corporations still had to earn your phone addiction and were more interested in selling your private info than building data centers in your backyard. Friend Request almost makes you miss the good old days, a feeling with which Michael De Santa is painfully familiar.

Michael is chopped. Michael is unc. Michael is miserable. After faking his death in the disastrous North Yankton job, the master criminal is “angrily decomposing” in his stately Los Santos manor, trapped in a world he never made with a family who doesn’t respect him. This is supposed to be the good life, a cushy retirement earned from years of risk and hard work, but Michael has never felt more hollow.

If the surface goal of Friend Request was to mock trends in tech and social media, the mission’s underlying purpose is to highlight Michael’s obsolescence, and in true Rockstar fashion, it’s not exactly subtle about it. Nearly every line of dialogue is a surgical strike on Michael’s self-worth.

He practically begs Lester to spin up a classic guns and ski-masks heist for old-time’s sake, only to be shot down in favor of sophisticated corporate espionage. He’s forced to buy lame clothes he doesn’t understand and suffers the shopgirl’s scornful side-eye. The fresh-faced peons at LifeInvader waiting for their shares to vest barely even register the middle-aged technician in their midst, even though they’re helpless to fix their computers without his expert clicking skills.

The dialogue makes the theme plain, but the lack of gameplay agency within the mission, while a Rockstar trope, also feeds the theme of Michael’s sense of inadequacy. Friend Request is built to shrink Michael, to heighten his midlife crisis and draw a contrast between the ambitious young Franklin and the unrepentant Trevor. He can’t sprint, shoot, or cause any overt trouble. He must play by this new society’s rules while gritting his teeth through the humiliation rituals of a future that’s left him behind.

Call Lester after leaving LifeInvader and the mastermind brags about his K/D/R in a violent shooter. Michael brushes it off, revealing his fondness for dusty Vinewood cinema instead, but it still stings a little. The man who sent us on the quest gets to actually have fun playing a video game while Michael is on a much-derided walk and follow mission, maybe the most hated archetype outside of escorting NPCs. Way to twist the knife!

The only catharsis for Michael comes at the very end of Friend Request, when his big man-of-action moment is reduced to pressing a button on his smartphone. The power in that single tap seems to rattle Michael, and the result of his fateful phone call reverberates throughout the game. LifeInvader stock plummets and never recovers, while a slate of optional assassinations allows players to further manipulate the economy and outright break it in their favor. Friend Request is the first step toward making money a complete non-issue in GTA V, and it's still not as satisfying as cracking open a vault and making a run for it. That will come soon enough.

It can be cope to defend something as intentionally boring, but it’s pretty clearly the case here. Missions that top the tier list feel like blockbuster action movies, but for every Die Hard there’s a delicious dull My Dinner With Andre. GTA’s legendary, long campaigns demand frequent changes of pace, and cooldown character studies like Friend Request offer exploration of a different kind than open-world adventure. Trekking through trauma, wandering through wounded pride, we’re given space to dig beneath the skin of the people we embody and understand what drives them.

Charlie "Moose" Lopresto graduated law school, passed the bar, and made a financially questionable decision to write about games and movies instead. Contributing to IGN since 2021, he collects solo board games and transforming robots.

articles.title: The Daggerheart: Hope & Fear Expansion Adds Tons of New Options to Critical Role's Daunting TTRPG
articles.body:
Critical Role’s TTRPG system, Daggerheart, puts a greater emphasis on story-telling than some of its peers. A year after the core book was released, Daggerheart offered players and Game Masters new options for telling their stories.with the system’s first expansion.

As someone who plays a variety of role-playing games on both sides of the GM screen, I’m always hungry for more options. More gear for my heroes to use and more vicious monsters to sic on my unsuspecting players.

Daggerheart: Hope and Fear adds a plethora of toys to the toybox, but if you weren’t a fan of the core book, don’t expect this expansion to change your mind.

Before diving into what’s new, for those unfamiliar, Daggerheart is a narrative-focused tabletop RPG system. It uses a rather handy card-based approach to help create and manage your characters and does away with the traditional initiative mechanic during combat. One of the most defining mechanics of Daggerheart, however, is its Hope and Fear dice.

These two twelve-sided dice, one representing your Hope value and the other Fear, can either cause your checks to earn you a 'Hope' resource that can be used to pull off extra special actions, or give your GM a 'Fear' point that they can spend. A proverbial "wrench in the gears" sort of treat, depending on which die rolls higher during the check. This mechanic also serves as the namesake for the system’s first expansion.

For players who have been wanting to make some new characters, a plethora of options await you inside this nearly 200-page tome. The Hope and Fear expansion comes with four new classes, each with two subclasses, six ancestries and communities, over 100 new pieces of gear and loot to dig through, and a brand-new domain. GMs get some new toys too, with 130+ new enemies to sic on those pesky heroes across 28 environments and four campaign frames (think of these as rough bases to build a campaign around). By far, though, my personal favorite inclusion in H&F is the brand-new Transformations system, but more on that gem in a bit.

The new domain, Dread, actually has some pretty interesting effects. The ones I found most intriguing and beneficial were abilities like Avatar of Terror, which makes you stronger the more Fear the GM has, and the spell Dire-Strike, which straight-up takes some of the GM’s Fear away. The idea that my friends and I could gang up and shut down the bullshit my GM might pull during a game instantly shot this new Domain to the top of my list for the next character I make.

Two new classes, the Assassin (a standalone, more stabby-focused rogue) and the Brawler (Daggerheart’s punchy monk-like class), utilize the core domains that came in the core book, while the other two new classes, the Warlock (make a pact with a thing, get cool powers) and the Witch (mess with enemies by hexing them), take advantage of H&F’s new Dread domain.

The new ancestries, which for D&D folks are basically Daggerheart’s equivalent to species, will feel familiar to anyone who’s played that other high-fantasy TTRPG. The Aetheris are winged, angel-y beings, while Elemental Kin—consisting of Earth, Ember (fire), Sky, and Tide (water) varieties—are individuals descended from powerful elementals. And then you have Gnomes, which are, well, gnomes.

All certainly good to have, but both the new ancestries and some of the new classes seem like such core fantasy staples that it feels odd to me that they weren’t included in the base release. Glad they’re here now, though, and gnomes being able to just teleport around with their Flicker Step feature is silly fun.

For the forever Game Masters out there (you are the real heroes), Hope & Fear’s new campaign frames offer good flexibility for running games for hesitant brand-new players or grizzled vets that want a challenge. My favorite out of the four offerings, surprisingly, is also the least complex: Castle High. Think modern-day wizard school where teenagers fly around on brooms while scrolling on their phones and take classes on giant floating islands in the sky. While I haven’t yet played or run the frame, the idea of swapping out my sword for pencil and paper and sneaking out of school instead of dungeons is a fun change of pace.

Of course, if you want to slay a dragon, or in this case a weredragon tyrant, you can do that too with Reign of the Weredragon. The most complex of the new offerings, Journey to Horizon, has you working to resurrect a goddess.

Now we can get to my favorite addition: transformations. Becoming a demigod, a werewolf, a vampire, or even living out your Danny Phantom dreams by transforming into a ghost is now possible! All of the transformation options in H&F (of which there are six) come with some sort of bonus or ability in addition to a downside. In Danny Phantom’s case, you take less physical damage but double magic damage, and can pass through solid objects at the cost of taking on some Stress.

I love transformations as a way to add further depth of your character or as a narrative plot thread, and the fact that they don’t count against any sort of domain or character limit (outside of only being allowed a single transformation at a time, but that’s what house rules are for) opens up all sorts of possibilities. Now, if Darrington Press could just make an official Super Sentai / Power Ranger transformation equivalent, I’d be all set! Castle High already features teenagers with attitude as the player characters, after all.

Daggerheart: Hope & Fear is a good first expansion, though it feels like a safe one. It adds a fair amount of new content for both players and GMs to mess around with, which is always great, even if some additions feel like they should have been included from the start. The Dread domain and how it can mess with the GM’s plans directly is a really fun twist. I’ve already gushed about the transformations, and I can’t wait to see what new options get added down the road.

That all said, since it launched, Daggerheart feels like a game that is far more intimidating to play for those who aren’t comfortable with improvisation and narrating what they are doing, and Hope & Fear doesn’t really help with that. I enjoy what it adds, but if you were already overwhelmed by the core game, don’t look to this expansion to save you. Daggerheart as a system is still, comparatively, in its infancy, and I would love to see a well-put-together starter kit or more hand-holdy expansion to help new players get into things.

articles.title: Stir the Scarecrow's Soul: How to Get the Scarecrow Song - The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Guide - IGN
articles.summary: There are many songs to learn on Link's journey in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. There's the iconic Zelda's Lullaby, Song of Time, and
articles.body:
There are many songs to learn on Link's journey in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. There's the iconic Zelda's Lullaby, Song of Time, and the warp songs that Sheik teaches Link before exploring each dungeon.

But there's one song from the game that is significantly less iconic because technically it doesn't actually exist. You get to make it.

The Scarecrow Song is a tune that is likely to vary from player to player, but it is a song that's obtainable in the game nonetheless. Here in the Switch 2 remake, the game even keeps track of it in your song list. But how exactly do you get the song and what is it used for?

In this quick guide, we'll show you everything you need to know about the Scarecrow Song in Ocarina of Time.

When you first visit Lake Hylia as Child Link, there's a field with a pair of scarecrows between the lakeside laboratory and the fishing pond.

Speak with the scarecrow closest to the water, Bonooru, who is wearing a green bandana. He'll want to hear a song you composed on the ocarina. So, pull out the instrument and play eight notes for him.

The song will be remembered exactly how you play it, including pauses. That means you can get creative . There are some limitations, however:

More than eight notes is too much for him to remember

Fewer than five notes is not significant enough for him to remember

You can't play one of the existing (or not yet obtained) songs

Whatever tune you go with, make sure it's not random and you can easily remember it, because it won't appear in your song list yet. You can then also play it to Pierre, the other scarecrow, who you will utlimately lend you a helping hand.

If you don't care about showing off your musical talents, you can go with something simple and easy to input, like: " L R L R L R L R "

Once you become an adult and are once again roaming Hyrule Field after seven long years, head back to Lake Halia. You'll find that now there's only one scarecrow here, the one with the green bandana.

Play your unique song for him to prove that you remember it. It will officially be added to your song list as it summons Pierre, the wandering scarecrow with the red bandana.

Piere will tell you to look out for spots where straw swirls in the wind because those are locations where he can be summoned.

Whenever you spot one of these swirls, noted as Scarecrow Spots on our maps, play your personal Scarecrow Song and Pierre will appear as a Hookshot target to reach faroff locations.

You may not find yourself using the song much simply to beat the game story. The song is mostly used for hidden Rupees and Pieces of Heart, special rewards that you have to go out of your way to obtain on a quest for 100% completion.

And that's everything there is to know about the scarecrow song in Ocarina of Time.

As a bonus, here are the keys to play an approximation of the Super Mario Bros. opening jingle.

articles.title: GTA 6 Will Do Something the Franchise Has Never Done Before: Encourage Empathy
articles.summary: Rockstar has confirmed GTA 6 features something the franchise has never had before: mechanisms that encourage empathy.
articles.body:
Rockstar has confirmed GTA 6 features something the franchise has never had before: mechanisms that encourage empathy.

Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson and head of publishing Jennifer Kolbe talked about how next week's Grand Theft Auto changes the formula the series is known for during an interview with The Guardian (via @GameRoll_ ). Jason and Lucia will surely be able to cause a fair amount of chaos when players take control in Vice City, but in a post- Red Dead Redemption 2 world, they'll have the freedom to be kind, too.

"Crime is a fundamental part of GTA – at least up until now, it has been," Nelson said. "We're trying to make sure we're not punishing people for playing the game they are used to … [but] your actions will have some effect on how the game plays out."

Games like GTA 5 have given players playgrounds and characters that can maximize the mayhem. Trevor, one of that game's three protagonists, is a great example of this chaotic energy, but in GTA 6, there doesn't seem to be a direct equivalent. Sure, Rockstar's trademark tone and instantly recognizable characters can be seen all over what few trailers we've received thus far, but everything seems a bit more grounded, too.

Falling in line with this is the news that GTA 6 will feature a world that might actually reward those who take the citizens of Leonida into consideration. Of course, that doesn't mean those who prefer to wreak havoc won't be able to play their way, too. It just means that, at least based on Nelson's words, there's some room to be a normal or even good person, too.

"I would say so," he replied when asked if the new game would encourage empathy in some capacity. "I would say that it's a product of the story we're trying to tell. We've tried for the first time in a GTA to provide mechanisms that encourage it, for those who want to."

In Pictures: How GTA 6's Jason and Lucia Have Evolved Since 2023

Elsewhere in the interview, Nelson described Jason and Lucia as a "younger couple with their backs against the wall," which is why it doesn't make sense for them to "go out and cause as much carnage and make as much noise as they can." This isn't Michael, Franklin, or Trevor, nor is it Niko Bellic. Thankfully, we won't have to wait too much longer to find out just what kind of criminals Jason and Lucia are, or who they can be.

GTA 6 launches November 19, 2026, for PS5 and Xbox Series X | S. With more grounded in-game mechanisms and NPCs that react to weapons, it's clear we're staring down what will likely be the most realistic Grand Theft Auto game so far. It's something that has plenty of fans excited and others nervous . Recent footage shared by Rockstar has highlighted the game's unbelievable graphics . It's something that has IGN writer Jacqueline Thomas excited , even if it does run at 30 fps .

articles.title: Chris Pratt Says He 'Would Love' James Gunn to Return for Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 4 After Leaving DC
articles.summary: Chris Pratt said he would love to reunite with James Gunn for Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 4 after the director abruptly announced he would be leaving DC Studios earlier this week.
articles.body:
Chris Pratt said he would love to reunite with James Gunn for Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 4 after the director abruptly announced he would be leaving DC Studios earlier this week.

Gunn is no longer running DC movies with Peter Safran – so what comes next? That's the question many comic book fans are asking as the dust begins to settle at Skydance, and although it will be quite a while before we actually see what happens, some are getting their hopes up for a Marvel reunion.

Gunn directed three Guardians of the Galaxy movies for the Marvel Cinematic Universe (and dealt with his fair share of drama ) while working with the Marvel Studios team before leaving to help head up DC Studios in 2022 . Work on Man of Tomorrow and one other mystery DC project aside , the comic book movie maker's future is wide open. Chris Pratt, who has starred as the MCU's Star-Lord for more than a decade, told Moviezine it would be "awesome" to re-team with Gunn for Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 4 now that DC is about nearly in the rearview mirror.

Hot Toys' Avengers: Doomsday Figures - Image Gallery

"That would be awesome. I love working with James. He's the man," Pratt said. "I haven't had a chance to speak with him since that news came out yesterday."

The last time we saw Star-Lord and the rest of the Guardians was in 2023's Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3 . Although that story fit well as a bookend for its characters and Gunn's work on the franchise, fans have had a hard time letting go of some of the MCU's most popular faces – Pratt included.

In January of this year, the actor said he has a "really strong vision" to bring Star-Lord back in future MCU installments. Just last month, he promised that plans for his return were in the works at Marvel Studios . Gamora actor Zoe Saldaña also said in 2024 that "it would be a huge loss" if the space-traveling heroes were left behind .

Gunn coming back to Marvel again feels like a long shot, and it's always possible that we could see the Guardians return in another MCU ensemble film like next year's Avengers: Secret Wars . At least for now, Pratt is willing to hold out hope.

"All I'll say is, I love James," he added. "He directed all three [Guardians of the Galaxy movies], and that's pretty rare in those types of trilogies, to have the same director through all three. If he wanted to come back and bring it back, man. I would love that."

Whether it's with the MCU or DC, much of the future is a mystery. In Gunn's case, we at least know Skydance has yet to even see his cut of Man of Tomorrow after the director squashed rumors claiming otherwise last night. We'll know about what's coming down the pipe for Marvel when Avengers: Doomsday arrives next month.

articles.title: Slick Rick Update - Steal An Egg [Roblox] Guide - IGN
articles.summary: The Slick Rick update includes a new area with eggs and pets to hatch, mutations, a new secret, and a dealer that you can purchase items from in Steal an Egg.
articles.body:
The Slick Rick update includes a new area with eggs and pets to hatch, mutations, a new secret, and a dealer that you can purchase items from in Steal an Egg . Available starting on Nov. 14, all players can expect to get involved in this update and reap the benefits. In this guide, we're going to break down everything included in the Slick Rick update in Steal an Egg.

Here's a thorough breakdown of everything new in the Slick Rick update.

The Slick Rick vendor operates the Black Market in Steal an Egg. Unlike other events or characters who have appeared in Steal an Egg, Slick Rick appears when he wants to show up. There's no set timer or specific window when he shows up. Instead, you'll have to wait for the notification to appear at the top of the screen, sharing Slick Rick's exact location and that he's available.

For now, Slick Rick appears inside the Alien Planet biome, and you need to reach the Lagoon to interact with him. He'll only be available for that day before disappearing, and you'll need to wait for that notification again. Slick Rick will have base customization options, weapons, and mutations available, along with the exclusive Blacklisted mutation.

The Stormlands is the new biome included in the Slick Rick update. You can find it at the center of the lane, between the Prehistoric and the Cosmic biome. You only need to be at least 150m speed to outrun the Guardian protecting this zone. As expected, there are eight new eggs for you to hatch, along with six exclusive ones that you can get from the Stormy Egg. You can get a Stormy Egg by spending Thunderstones, which appear during the Skyfall event.

Here's a breakdown of all the available eggs and pets from the Stormlands biome.

Here are the exclusive pets you can get from the Stormy Egg in the Stormlands biome. Unlike other exclusive pets for limited eggs, the chances to acquire any of these pets are not listed.

The Skyfall event exclusively happens in the Stormlands biome. It happens every 30 minutes, on the hour and half-hour time marks. When this happens, thunderstones fall from the sky in that zone. You'll need to head over there with your hammer and begin destroying them. You'll acquire thunderstones that you can use to purchase the Stormy Egg, but there's a chance these stones can reward you with Storm Glass.

Storm Glass is a rare material that you can take to the Stormheart Cave and charge the mysterious device at this location. You'll need at least three of them to start it up.

You can find the Stormheart Cave at the center of the Stormlands biome. You can head inside at any time, where you'll find a mole named Rumble and the Storm Conductor. If you want to use the Storm Conductor, you need to provide it with three Storm Glass that you can get from the Skyfall event. When the Storm Conductor is activated, you'll fly into the air and be able to collect Sparks that the conductor shoots out.

You can exchange 150 Sparks with Rumble to get a Thunderous Mutation that you can place on your eggs.

articles.title: 'It Felt Criminal' — Adam Driver Still Can't Believe How Disney Handled Canceled Star Wars Movie The Hunt for Ben Solo
articles.summary: Adam Driver still can't believe Disney killed his Star Wars movie, The Hunt for Ben Solo, and has now gone so far as to say that the move "felt criminal."
articles.body:
Adam Driver still can't believe Disney killed his Star Wars movie, The Hunt for Ben Solo, and has now gone so far as to say that the move "felt criminal."

The Kylo Ren/Ben Solo actor relived some of the darker parts of his past with the massive sci-fi franchise during a recent conversation with AP . His updated thoughts on the matter follow years of work and months of fan organizing, and although he and director Steven Soderbergh have almost nothing to show for it, he's still pretty fired up about how it all went down.

"For me it was: Steven Soderbergh wants to make a Star Wars film," Driver said. "What are we debating? It’s what it is. It’s criminal. Or it felt criminal. We’re all moving on. On to the next. And Steven already has something else that’s one of the best things he’s ever written."

How Much Every Star Wars Movie Made Opening Weekend

We first learned about The Hunt for Ben Solo, a Skywalker Saga follow-up that explored a potential future for its title character, when Driver called it one of the "coolest scripts" he had "ever been a part of" late last year. Despite the hype, it never came to be, mostly because, according to Driver, then-Disney CEO Bob Iger and co-chairman Alan Bergman "didn't see how Ben Solo was alive."

What followed was months of additional words from those who worked on the shuttered project, including Soderbergh, who called Disney's decision to pull the plug after two-and-a-half years of work "insane." Before long, fans orchestrated their own campaign to try and save the movie , but at least as far as August 2026, Lucasfilm president Dave Filoni has said that it's not something the company is working on right now .

With so much work put into it, it's been hard for many to see why Disney would shut down an impassioned pitch from a fan-favorite Star Wars actor. Driver himself still seems confused about the call to this day. The silver lining, though, was how dedicated fans chipped in to see his and Soderbergh's ideas brought to life.

George Lucas Would Have Killed Luke Skywalker and Other Weird Star Wars Facts

"I was blown away by the response to it," Driver added. "In no way did I think there would be billboards in Times Square. It’s so moving. It did feel like we were all at the bar having a conversation about the films we wanted to see."

For now, however, Driver is most likely hanging up his hilted lightsaber for good. He said as much during another interview earlier this month, though he's still leaving the door open should Disney change its mind about The Hunt for Ben Solo . Soderbergh, who is currently helping out with The Batman Part 2 , ruled out a return in April of this year.

Taika Waititi's long-gestating Star Wars movie joined the Ben Solo film when it was officially put on ice last month . While Star Wars' future has plenty of question marks to address , there are a few projects confirmed to launch in the next year alone. You can see IGN's full breakdown for every movie and show in development here .

Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

articles.title: Miami’s Malachi Toney Draws Attention With Pregame Appearance While Sidelined
articles.summary: The Miami Hurricanes are taking the field without Malachi Toney against Duke, but their injured receiver still found a way to get attention before kickoff. T...
articles.body:
The Miami Hurricanes are taking the field without Malachi Toney against Duke, but their injured receiver still found a way to get attention before kickoff. Toney was reportedly among the first Miami players to arrive at Hard Rock Stadium on Saturday. He had a walking boot on, and he was playing catch.

Jordan Lopez reported the sighting Saturday morning. For Hurricanes fans waiting to see Toney back in action, it was a chance to see him around the team on game day. The boot, though, was a reminder that his recovery remains part of the story.

Malachi Toney Shows Up Early Before Miami Faces Duke

There is something fans can appreciate about an injured player showing up early when he knows he will not be playing. Game day looks different without the usual preparation for snaps, catches and matchups. Toney nevertheless made it to the stadium ahead of many of his teammates, according to the report. That is a telling update.

Playing catch makes the appearance more interesting than simply seeing him on the sideline. It gives Miami supporters something to discuss while they wait for another update. It does not, however, tell them when he will be cleared to compete again.

Toney's ankle injury had already changed the conversation around Miami's offense. The Associated Press reported earlier this month that he needed surgery for a high ankle sprain and would miss multiple weeks. That left the Hurricanes preparing to move forward without a receiver who had become a major part of their identity.

Miami Still Has Work to Do Without Its Star Receiver

For now, the football question is how Miami handles the opportunities that remain available in his absence. Losing an important target asks more of the quarterback, the other receivers and the coaches calling the offense. Nobody gets to pause the schedule while a teammate recovers.

That is why Saturday's appearance offers a lighter moment without answering the bigger question. Toney was present, he was throwing the ball around, and fans had something besides an injury designation to talk about. Those details can be welcome without turning them into a prediction.

Miami supporters would prefer to see him wearing cleats and getting ready to play. Until that happens, the meaningful updates will concern his medical clearance and availability. His early arrival against Duke offered a glimpse of his Saturday routine while everyone waits for that next step.
